sections.label: Mind
sections.text:
Great loquacity. Amative. Sad in the morn-
ing; no desire to mix with the world. Restless and un-
easy; does not wish to attend to business; wants to be
off somewhere all the time. Jealous. Mental

labor best performed at night. Religious insanity.
[Vcrat.: Stram.] Derangement of the time sense.

sections.label: Head
sections.text:
Pain through head on awaking. Pain at root
of nose Pressure and burning on vertex. Waves of
pain ; worse after moving. Sun headaches. With head-
ache, very pale face. Vertigo.

sections.label: Eyes
sections.text:
Defective vision after diphtheria, extrinsic
nluscles too weak to maintain focus. Sensation as if
eyes were drawn together by cords which were tied in
a knot at root of nose.

sections.label: Ears
sections.text:
Tearing pain from zygoma into ear; also with
sore throat. Ear-wax hard, dry.

sections.label: Nose
sections.text:
Bleeding, nostrils sensitive. Coryza, preceded
by headache. Hay asthma; paroxysms of sneezing.
[Silica.; Sabad.]

sections.label: Face
sections.text:
Pale. Trifacial neuralgia, left side, heat run-
ning up into head. [PAoj.] Tearing pain in jaw-bones.
[Amphishoena; Phos.] Purple, mottled, puffed; looks
swollen, bloated, jaundiced, chlorotic.

sections.label: Mouth
sections.text:
Gums swollen, spongy, bleed. Tongue
swollen, burns, trembles, red, dry and cracked at tip,
catches on teeth. Aphthous and denuded spots with
burning and rawness. Nauseous taste. Teeth ache,
pain extends to turs. Pain in facial bones.

446

sections.label: Throat
sections.text:
Quinsy. Dry, intensely swollen, externally
and internally. Diphtheria ; membrane dusky, blackish ;
pain aggraz^atcd by hot drinks; chronic sore throat, with
much hawking; mucus sticks, and cannot be forced up
or down. Very painful; worse slightest pressure, touch
is even more annoying. Worse on left side. In diph-
theria, etc., the trouble began on the left side. Tonsils
purplish. Purple, livid color of throat. Feeling as if
something was swollen which must be swallowed ; zvorsc,
swallowing saliva or liquids. Pain into ear. Collar and
neck-band must be very loose.

sections.label: Stomach
sections.text:
Craving for alcohol, oysters. Any food
causes distress. Pit of stomach painful to touch. Hun-
gry, cannot wait for food. Gnawing pressure made bet-
ter by eatipg, but returning in a few hours. Perceptible
trembling movement in the epigastric region. Empty
swallowing more painful than swallowing solids.

sections.label: Abdomen
sections.text:
Liver region sensitive, cannot bear any-
thing around waist. Especially suitable to drunkards.*"
Abdomen tympanitic, sensitive, painful. [Bell.]

sections.label: Stool
sections.text:
Constipated, offensive stool. Anus feels tight,
as if nothing could go through it. Pain darting up the
rectum every time he sneezes or coughs. Haemorrhage
from bowels like charred straw, black particles.
Haemorrhoids protrude, become constricted, purplish.
Stitches in them on sneezing or coughing. Constant
urging in rectum, not for stool.

sections.label: Female
sections.text:
Climacteric troubles, palpitation, flashes of
heat, haemorrhages, vertex headache, fainting spells;
worse, pressure of clothes. Menses too short, too
feeble; pains all relieved hy the flow. [Eupion.] Left
ovary very painful and swollen, indurated. Mammae in-
flamed, bluish. Coccyx and sacrum pain, especially on
,^^ng from sitting posture. Acts especially well at be-
' Ifinning and close of menstruation.


447

sections.label: Male
sections.text: Intense excitement of sexual organs.

sections.label: Respiratory
sections.text:
Upper part of windpipe very suscepti-
ble to touch. Sensation of suffocation and strangulation
on lying down, particularly when anything is around
throat; compels patient to spring from bed and rush
for open window. Spasm of glottis; feels as if some-
thing ran from neck to larynx. Feels he must take a
deep breath. Cramp-like distress in prsecordial region.
Cough ; dry, suffocative fits, tickling. Little secretion
and much sensitiveness ; worse, pressure on larynx,
after sleep, open air. Breathing almost stops on falling
asleep. [Grind.] Larynx painful to touch. StMisation
as of a plug [Ahac.] which moves up and down, with a
short cough.

sections.label: Heart
sections.text:
Palpitation, with fainting spells, especially
during climacteric. Constricted feeling, causing palpita-
tion, with an.xiety. Cyanosis. Irregular beats.

sections.label: Back
sections.text:
Neuralgia of coccyx, tvorse rising from sitting
posture; must sit perfectly still. Pain in neck, worse
cervical region.

sections.label: Sleep
sections.text:
Patient sleeps into an aggravation. Sudden
starting when falling .sleep. Sleepiness, yet cannot

sections.label: sleep
sections.text: [Bell.; Op.] Wide-awake in evening.

sections.label: Fever
sections.text:
Chilly in back ; feet icy cold ; hot flushes and
hot perspiration. Paroxysm returns after acids. Inter-
mittent fever every spring.

sections.label: Skin
sections.text:
Hot perspiration, bluish, purplish appearance.
Boils, carbuncles, ulcers, with bluish, purple surround-
ings. Dark blisters. Bed-sores, with black edges. Blue-
black swellings. Pyaemia; dissecting wounds. Purpura,
with intense prostration. Senile erysipelas. Wens.
Cellulitis.

sections.label: Modalities
sections.text:
Worse, after sleep, (Kali bich.) Lach-
esis sleeps into aggravation; left side, in the spring,

448


warm bath, pressure or constriction, hot drinks. Better,
appearance of discharges, warm applications.

sections.label: Relationship
sections.text:
Antidotes: Ars.; Merc.; Heat; Alco-
hol; Salt.

Complementary: Lycop.; Hep.; Salamandra.

Incompatible: Acet. ac.; Carb. ac.

Compare: Cotyledon (climacteric troubles); Nat. m..
Nit. ac.; Crotal.; Amphisboena — snake lizard — (right
jaw swollen and painful, lancinating pains; headaches,
lancinating pains. Eruption of vesicles and pimples) ;
Naja; Scolo pendra — Centipede — (malignant pustule;
angina pectoris). Lepidium (affections of the breast,
heart, lancinating pains).

sections.label: skin
sections.text:
The mere touch of the skin with the finger or hand is unbearable.

There are many inflammatory and congestive conditions of the eyes.
The eye symptoms are worse after sleep, and the eyes are oversensi-
tive to touch and light. With the eye symptoms we have headaches,
because the brain and eyes arc so closely associated. In the sore,
throats, when the spatula or tongue depressor happens to touch the
wall of the throat, the tonsil, or the root of the tongue, there is a feeling
as if the eyes would be pressed out. Violent pain in the eyes fromi
touching the throat. Lachesis is a great jaundice medicine, because
it produces much disturbance in the liver. Yellowness of the skin and
whites of the eyes, and thickening of tissues about the eyes. “Fistula
lachrymalis,’' which is accompanied by long standing eruptions about
the face.

Oversensitiveness of the meatus auditorus externus. Anything in-
troduced into the canal of the ear will cause violent, spasmodic cough-
ing and tickling in the throat. So sensitive is the mucous membrane
of the ear that a violent cough, like whooping cough, will come on £rom>
touching the mucous membrane of the ear. This only shows the over-
sensitiveness of reflexes, and the oversensitiveness in general. With
the hearing there is the same oversensitiveness that we have spoken
of elsewhere. The Eustachian tube becomes closed with a catarrhal
thickening, stricture of the Eustachian tube.

The catarrhal symptoms of the nose are prominent. F requent
bleeding of the nose ai^ b ody, wa te ry discharge from the nose. Always
taking cold tiT the nose. St uffing up of the nose, with disturbance of
smell. O ycrsensitiy en^.s to sm ell, and^pver^sit ive ness to odors.
finally loss of smell. Lachesis has inflammatory conditions, very
'eftronte^ with crusty formations in jdie nose, sneezing,

watery disc harges from the nose and catarrhal headac hes. S ometimes
tEe“liea3acEe goes off when th e catarrhal discharge comes. a ndT when the
"cafaifh^'disc^^^ headache comes on. Violent headache

with dischafigeT mth sneezing and coryza. Congestive headaches with
coryza. This catarrhal condition has led to the use oT Lachesis in

lACHESlS

605

syphilis. It is sufficiently similar to cope with the severe forms of nasal
syphilis ; syphilis where it has affected the nasal mucous membrane,
producing crusts and finally affecting the bones. Focid ozcena ; very
offensive discharges from the nose. Bleeding from the nose need not
surprise you, because Lachesis is a hai^morrhagic remedy. The blood
from the nose or any part, when it dries or clots, looks like charred
straw or becomes black. Parts bleed easily. Copious and prolonged
uterine haemorrhage, copious and prolonged menstruation, bleeding
from the nose, vomiting of blood, haemorrhage from the bowels in
typhoids. ‘'Great sensitiveness of the nostrils and lips, swelling of
the lips, great swelling and tumefaction of the nose in old cases of
syphilis."' The nose swells up and becomes purple. The nasal bones
are very sore, soreness upon sides of the nose. Lachesis is an espe-
cially useful medicine in old drunkards who have red nose, and in
heart affections with red nose. A red knob on the end of the nose, a
strawberry nose.

The face is purple and mottled, the eyelids are tumid, very much
puffed ; not bloated as in oedematous subjects, but puffed. There is not
the pitting upon pressure that we find in cedema, although Lachesis
has that, but there is a puffiness peculiar to Lachesis, fhe f ace loo ks
swollen and inflamed , due to a venous stasis, so that the face is purple
and mottled. Thc^no se is tumid, je t i t will not reniain pitted upon
pre ssure. The lips feel as if inflamed, yet are not inflamed, simply
sensitive to pressure. The face has also an oedematous appearance in
which there is pitting upon pressum, in cardiac affections, in cases of
Bright’s disease. On the other hmd the face becomes very pale, pale
and cold ; the skin covered with scaly eruptions. Eruptions that bleed
easily, with crusty eruptions, with vesicular eruptions. Eruptions that
fill with blood, bloody vesicles and large blood blisters, such as occur
sometimes in burns, with burning. The face becomes jaundiced and
very sallow. At times it takes on the appearance also of a chlorosis.
If you have once seen the chlorotic color, it need not be described. It
is a condition of anaemia, with yellowish pallor, ash colored or grey,
intermingled with a sort of greenish color, so that the ancients often
referred to it as green sickness. Again the face becomes livid and
puffed like the bloated aspect of drunkards, the mottled purple appear-
ance of drunkards who have been drinking for years, until they are
bloated and broken down and have a besotted aspect. You see that in,

In Lachesis we have a remedy for erysipelas and gangrenous affec-
tions, and about the affected part there is the Lachesis appearance,
that is the mottled, purplish appearance. Lachesis has become clinically
a marked remedy for erysipelas and for gangrene. As provers do not
follow up remedies until they produce these things, we have to gather^

6o6

tACH£StS

them from the poisonous effects and clinical observation.

In Lachesis there is oozing of blood around the teeth) the gums
bleed easily. Dry crusts appear upon the teeth in zymotic diseases,
often black formations, sordes, and the tongue takes part in the appear-
ance of the mouth and becomes slick. This occurs in typhoid condi-
tions when there is a total loss of assimilation, the appetite is entirely
gone, the stomach will not take food, and when food is put into the
stomach it is rejected. There is also paresis of the tongue. The
tongue seems to be like leather in the mouth, it is moved with great
difficulty. And the speech is like that of one half intoxicated :
he is unable to articulate. The tongue swells and is protruded very
slowly. It is dry and catches on the teeth and seems to have lost its
stiffness. Seems like a rag, or as if the muscles did not act upon it so
that it cannot be protruded, or if it is protruded it trembles and quivers
and jerks and catches on the teeth. Again it is swollen, it is denuded
of its papillae, and smooth, shiny and glassy as if varnished. In the
mouth there is a soapy appearance of the saliva. The saliva runs into
the mouth copiously and the patient will often lie with the head over
the side of the bed, and the saliva dripping into a pan or commode.
The saliva is stringy and can be pulled out of the mouth in strings ;
white mucus or saliva. This is not an uncommon feature in diphtheria,
in sore throat, in inflammation of the tongue and mouth and gums, and
in inflammation of the salivary glands. When this mucus is thick,
tough, yellow, stringy and ropy it is like Kali bichromicum. You will
often find in severe sore throat that the patient will lie and gag, and
cough, and attempt with difficulty to protrude the tongue to expel the
saliva from the mouth. Very often the pain is so severe in the root of
the tongue that he cannot expel the saliva by the tongue and he will lie
with the open mouth over a commode, or with a cloth over the pillow,
to receive the thick, ropy saliva. In such a state with sore throats,
especially those that commence on the left side and go to the right,
you hardly need to question longer, for it is the aspect of Lachesis.
This state of affairs would lead to Lachesis in ordinary inflammatory
conditions of the tongue and in cancerous affections of the tongue.
Lach. has in its nature the tendency to formation of malignant scabs
and malignant ulcers, such as we find in epithelioma. It has cured a
number of cases of epithelioma. It has been a very useful remedy in
lupus. It is an important remedy in syphilitic sore throat, in syphilitic
ulceration of the throat, tongue and roof of the mouth with this
copious, stingy saliva.

The muscles of the pharynx become paralyzed and will not act, and
hence the food will collect in the pharynx, that is, the bolus to bo
swallowed goes to the pharynx and stops, and then a tremendous effort
at swallowing, with gagging and coughing and spasmodic action of the


607

chest, takes place in order to carry on respiration, and he will not again
attempt it. This state often occurs with diphtheria. I have a number
of times seen it brought about by the physician, who has, instead of
giving just enough Lachesis, high enough and similar enough to the
disease to cure, given it as low as he could get it, the 8th or loth, dis-
solved it in water and fed it all through the diphtheritic state. When
you come across cases that have been treated in this way you need not
be surprised if a post-diphtheritic paralysis comes on, because Lachesis
will produce it. It may cure the diphtheria, but it will leave its poison-
ous effects which will last that patient a lifetime. Every spring the
symptoms of Lachesis will crop out. In all the circumstances of aggra-
vation described the symptoms of Lachesis will crop out if he has once
been poisoned by it.

In the sore throat we have a combination of symptoms. Lachesis
has produced this state, going from left to right : but with the sore
throat there is a sensation of fulness in the neck and throat, difficult
breathing, pallor or plethoric appearance of the face, choking when
going into sleep, the peculiar kind of saliva and aggravation of the
throat symptoms from warm drinks. There is not always an aggrava-
tion of the pain itself from warm drinks, but the patient is often unable
to swallow warm fluids. The swallowing of warm fluids often causes
choking, and after a swallow of warm tea is taken the patient will
clutch at the throat and it seems if he would suffocate. He says,
“Ohl do not give me any more w*rra drinks.” Something cold will
relieve. The dyspnoea and the distress about the throat is increased
by swallowing something warm. Now, in the sore throats of Lycopo*
dium, warmth often benefits, but it is also true in some cases of Lyco-
podium sore throat, they want ctfld drinks and cold feels good to the

Very often in the more acute symptoms of Lachesis a warm drink in
the stomach is hurtful and causes nausea and suffocation and increases
the choking and palpitation and the fulness in the head, whereas in the
chronic cases of Lachesis, those that have been poisoned years before,
there will be a sensation of nausea and tendency to vomit from taking a
drink of cold water and then lying down. The nausea comes on after
lying down, that is, let the patient take a drink of ice cold water and go
to bed and nausea will come on. Such a state is peculiar to Lachesis.
It has been a later observation of those who have long before proved
lachesis. The symptoms of Lachesis have sometimes to be taken'
years after.

Lachesis has ulcers in the throat. It has aphthous patches, it has red
and grey ulceration, it has deep ulceration. The tendency to ulceration
upon the margins of mucous membranes is peculiar to Lachesis. Also
ulceration upon the skin, where the circulation is feeble. It seems that

6o8


the pain in the throat is particularly marked between the acts of swal-
lowing, and the pressure of the bolus going over the inflamed tonsils
relieves the pain. Always choking when swallowing, choking and gag-
ging in the throat. The cough is a choking cough and produces a sen-
sation of tickling. This is like the Bell cough. Bell antidotes a Lach.
cough, it has a cough so much like Lach. that no one can tell them apart.
Again the throat takes on extreme dryness in Lach., and this dryness is
without thirst, dryness with aversion to water. Much inclination to
swallow ; the tendency is to continuously swallow, yet it is painful.
Empty swallowing is more painfull than the swallowing of solids. Some
Lach. patients suffering from cardiac affections are annoyed with con-
striction of the throat, choking in the throat when anything warm is
swallowed, and sometimes when going into a warm room, choking and
palpitation of the heart. Tendency to chronic sore throat or recurrent
sore throat and ulceration with every recurring sore throat. Liquids,
of course, you will see, arc analogous to empty swallowing, and empty
swallowing causes more pain than the bolus which presses upon the
sore throat, because it is of the nature of a slight touch. The slight
touch increases the soreness and pain in the throat. Slight pressure of
the collar increases the pain in the throat. With the sore throat the
muscles and glands about tlie neck become painful, inflamed and swoll-
en, and very tender to the touch. With the sore throat, very com-
monly, there is pain in the base of the brain or in the back of the head,
and soreness of the muscles of the back of the neck, which is often re-
lieved by lying on the back and aggravated by lying on either side. If
you look into the throat it has a mottled, purplish appearance. Put all
these things together, with the copious flow of tenacious saliva, and
you will be able to manage cases of diphtheria that commence on the
left side and spread to the right, whether the membrane is scanty or
copious. Tonsilitis with suppuration of the tonsils, when the left tonsil
becomes inflamed and after a day or two the right one becomes inflamed
and swollen, and they both finally go on to suppuration, or when one
swells and suppurates and the other swells and suppurates. Diphther-
itic appearances of the throat, spreading from left to right. The
pharynx is full of thick, white, ropy mucus in the morning ; must hawk
out a mouthful of mucus in the morning.

The abdomen is distended with flatus. The abdomen is tympanitic
in typhoid condition, much rumbling in the distended abdomen. The
clothing cannot be tolerated, not even the slightest touch of the clothing,
and yet it may require hard pressure to bring out soreness that is deep
in the abdomen. This state is as it is in inflammation of bowels, ovaries
and uterus, the patient lies on the back with the clothing lifted from the

Lach. has a series of liver troubles with jaundice ; congestion of the
liver, inflammation of the liver, enlarged liver and the nutmeg liver.
Cutting like a knife in the region of the liver. Vomiting of bile ; vomit-
ing of everything taken into the stomach. Extreme nausea ; continuous
nausea witih jaundice. White stool. It has cured cases with gall stone.
“Cannot endure any pressure about the hypochondria.” In the chronic
state the sensitiveness of the skin is so great over the abdomen, and
about the waist and hips, that the wearing of the clothing creates pain,
great restlessness and uneasiness, the patient grows increasingly ner-
vous and finally goes into hysterics. Sensitiveness over the lower
abdomen ; can scarcely allow her clothes to touch her.

It seems strange at first reading that Lachesis can be such a common
remedy at the menstrual period. It is also laid down as a remedy for
the climacteric period. Now if you will study the cases of many
women at the climacteric period you will find that many of them have
the flushes of heat and the surgings in the head and the great circula-

the complaints, the headaches, etc., that come in women at the climac-

sections.label: Nose

Objective. Margins of the nostrils red, sore, erysipelatous ;
with catarrh,'. — After catarrh, the nose remains red and sore in the angles

Na.-ial mucus (fifteenth day), preceded by mucus in the throat,". — Yellow

and cough, with easily loosened expectoration, with moderate heat of the
head and hands, dim eyes, violent palpitation of the heart, together with

and has to strain a great deal, at 5.45 p.m. (after a quarter of an hour) ;
has usually one regular evacuation in the morning, none in the afternoon
(first day),^ — Bowels moved twice, morning and night (second day) ; twice
in the morning (third day),^

Urinary Organs. — Pressing in the bladder during micturition
(after two hours and a half, first day),'. — Some drops flow out of the
urethra, coloring the shirt red, during the night (tenth day),'.

Sexual Organs. — Strong burning in the left half of the scrotum,
extending towards the right side (after two hours, second day),'.

Respiratory Organs. — [120,] Burning in the right side of the
larynx (fourth day),'. — ^Short cough, with sore throat, at night in bed (third
day) ; worse in bed and preventing sleep (fourth and fiifth days) ; slight
(sixth day) ; a little, in morning (ninth day) ; some, in evening (tenth
day),*.

sections.label: Chest
sections.text:
Feels full in the chest, and this compels him to take a long
breath (after three-quarters of an hour, third day),'. — Felt hot in the chest
and around the heart (after five minutes, third day),'. — Awakens at 2 a.m.
with a crampy pain in the chest extending from the right to the left side ;
afterwards pain in the forehead, with general heat alternating with the
above-mentioned pain in the chest; at last it moves into the neck and
shoulders (first night),^ — Stitches in the left side of the chest (seventh
day),'. — Stitches as with a knife in quick succession, in the right side of the
chest under the right breast ; motion or rest has no influence ; afterwards
stitches as with knives in the region of the left collar-bone, after midnight
(second night) ; again under the right breast, at 8 a.m. (third dstj),'. — Boil-
ing and bubbling in the chest and the region of the heart ; it ascends up to
the head and makes him quite giddy ; breaks out into perspiration (after
three-quarters of an hour, second day),'.

Heart and Pulse. — Sensation of heat in the region of the heart,
going and coming (after fifteen minutes, third day),'. — When lying, he feels
the beating of his heart to his head (after three hours and three-quarters,
third day),'.— [130.] Pulse 54, at 5 p.m. (fourth day),'.— Pulse 58 (after
six hours, first day) ; 60 (after one hour and a quarter, second day) ; 64,
in the morning (third day),'. — Pulse 60 (after three-quarters of an hour) ;
74, some beats are slow, others are fast (after one hour and three-quarters);
54 (after three hours and three-quarters) ; 68 (after six hours and three-
quarters) ; 76 (after twelve hours and a quarter, third day),'. — Pulse 84
(before taking) ; 80 (after twenty minutes) ; 72, after lying down and sleep-
ing (two hours and twenty minutes after first dose, first day) ; 74 (on tak-
ing second dose) ; 58 (four hours after second dose, fourth day) ; 86 (fifth
day),l

NecTt and BacJc. — Wecle. *Stiffness of the neck (fifth day),'. — Pain
in the neck and shoulders (first night),^ — Pain and stiffness in the neck,
going over the whole head down to the nose, then like pinching the nostrils
together (after one hour, second day),'. — Pain in the nape of the neck, as
if from dislocation, when turning the neck or bending the head backward
(after two hours, second day),'. — Back. Burning in the spine, about four
inches above the small of the back (after one hour and a half, second day),'.
— Sensation of pressure under the short ribs of the right side of the back,
deepseated, while taking a long breath (after three-quarters of an hour,

ing in the region of the left kidney, deep internally, drawing towards the

Burning in the juncture of the ilium with the sacrum, deep internally,
drawing towards the right (after three-quarters of an hour) ; soon after
burning in the region of the left kidney, deep internally, drawing towards
the right side (second day),'. — Tearing in the right ischium (second day) ;
deep inside (after three-quarters of an hour, third day),'.

Extremities in General. — Tearing in the limbs (twenty-fourth
and twenty-fifth days),*.

Superior Extremities. — Tearing in the left upper arm from the
elbow-joint to the shoulder-joint ; it pains most in the elbow-joint (after five
hours and a half, first day),'. — [150.] Tearing in both elbow-joints, some-
times upwards, then downwards, frequently through the day (seventh day),'.
— Tearing in the left elbow-joint (after one hour, second day),'. — Tearing
in the right arm below the elbow (eighth day),'. — It drew the left index
finger crooked (after one hour and a half, first day),'. — Tearing in the
knuckles of the middle fingers of the right hand (tenth day),'.

Infer ioi' Extremities. — Thigh. Burning on the right thigh, far
up on the inside (after three-quarters of an hour, third day),'. — JLnee,
Pains below the left knee-pan (seventh day),'. — Tearing in the right knee-,
while walking (tenth day),'. — Tearing in the right knee-cap (ninth day),'. —
Tearing in the left knee (tenth day),'. — £ef/. [160.] Tingling in both
lower legs and feet, through and through, but worse in the calf (second
day),'. — ^Tearing in the right tibia (eighth day) ; in the afternoon (fourth
day),'. — Cramp (spasm) in the right calf, in the morning when lying
in bed (fourth day),'. — Foot. While running, suddenly a sensation as
if the left foot was out of joint, so that he stumbles, afterwards tearing in
the joint of the left foot (fourth day),'. — Stitch behind the right exter-
nal malleolus (after three hours, first day),l — Cramp in the left foot, con-
tinuing for half an hour, about 9 A.M. (sixth day),*. — Cramp in the left
foot, at night (seventeenth night),*. — Toes. Burning in the left big toe
(after one hour and three-quarters, third day),'. — Burning under the nail
of the left toe (after one hour, first day),'. — Tearing in the right big toe,
waking him from his sleep (sixth night),'-

General Sym'ptotns. — [170.] Feels weak (ninth day),*.— Restless,
throws herself about (first night),^ — Very restless while perspiring (eleventh
night),*.

Shin. — Objective. Appearance of some few little pimples in the
bends of the elbows (fifth day),'. — On the left gluteus muscle just on the
point is formed a pimple with hard red circumference of the size of a penny,
is very painful, when touched exceedingly sore, afterwards burning (sixth
day) ; the pimple does not break, but is very painful (tenth day) ; a few
more pimples formed around the gluteus muscle, they itch, and when
opened by scratching ooze out some watery substance (eleventh day),'. —
On the forehead elevated red pimples (fifteenth day) ; they become larger
and suppurate (sixteenth day),*. — Subjective. Itching and burning of

Burning and itching on the right knee, which looks scarlet-red (third

on the right elbow-joint, continues for several days, and is worse in the

Sleep and Dreams, — Sleepiness. Drowsiness during the day
(twenty-fourth and twenty-fifth days),* — Sleeplessness. [190.] Cannot
go to sleep early, contrary to his habit (fifth day),'. — Awakens often during
the night, contrary to his habit (second night),'. — During the night she is over-
wakeful without much difiiculty (symptoms?), (twenty-fourth and twenty-
fifth days),*. — Restless sleep at night, followed by perspiration (first night),*.
— Little and restless sleep, during the night (third night),*. — No sleep be-
fore midnight (eleventh night),*. — No sleep till morning, when she has
feverish distressing dreams (eighteenth night),*. — Sleepless (first eighteen
nights, except sixteenth night, and twentieth, twenty-first, and twenty-
second nights),*. — Dreains. Distressing dreams every night (fifth day),*.
— Dreams that she is spinning, and marked her yarn with red wool (first
night),'''. — [200.] When sleeping, she sees all kinds of images (twenty-fourth
and twenty-fifth da3's),*.

sections.label: Fever
sections.text:
Chilliness. Body icy cold, she cannot get warm, although
one hour and a half under a feather-bed ; head burns like fire, with much
thirst (during headache) ; (eighth and ninth days),*. — Heat. She feels hot
and oppressed in chest, with mild perspiration all over, of short duration
(after four hours and a half, first day),'. — General heat alternating with
crampy pain in the chest (first night),^ — Burning heat, with redness of the
face, more on the right side ; after the heat had ceased circumscribed dark
redness of the cheeks, worse on the right side, in the afternoon (twelfth
day),*. — Dry heat; the feet burn, she is restless, throws herself about; much
rumbling in the abdomen (first night),^ — Flushes of heat alternating with
chilliness (nineteenth day),*.— Feverish, at 8 p.m. (nineteenth day),*.—
Fever from 6 to 12 p.m., then better, with redness of the face, and more on
the upper part of the face (twenty-fourth and twenty-fifth days),*.— Burn-
ing in the palms of the hands and soles of the feet (twenty-fourth and
twenty-fifth days)*.— Sweat. [210.] Breaks out into perspiration (after
three-quarters of an hour, second day),'. — Perspiration, following restless
sleep (first night),*. — Perspiration and itching of the penis and scrotum, for
some days (fifth day),'.— Much perspiration after midnight (eleventh
night) ; continued perspiration, in the morning (twelfth day),*. — Dxiring
the cold sensation, the skin is moist and sticky (eighth and ninth days),*.

Preparation for use. Dilutions.

Authorities. 1, Dr. S. Swan, proving with the 15th dil., obtained from
Dr. Reisig (Note : The preparation was doubtless sour milk, and not pure
lactic acid), drop doses every hour for ten hours, N. Am. J. of Hom., 1871,
p. 569; 2, same, effects of 30th, in a lady-patient, reported by Dr. B. Fincke;
3, same, effects of 30th, in Dr. B. Fincke (Nos. 4 to 18, provings by T. F.
Allen, with pure acid, N. Y. J. of Horn., 1, p. 337) ; 4, J. H. Buffum, two doses
of 30th dil. ; 5, W. H. T., 30th dil. ; 6, F. R., 30th dil. ; 7, E. S. M., 30th
dil. ; 8, 0. A. S., 30th dil. ; 9, J. P. W., 30th dil. ; 10, J. R. P., 30th dil. ; 11,

Dr. Simmons, Jr., 30th dil. ; 15, A. W. J., two provings, each with one dose
of 30th dil. ; 16, F. R., several doses of 1st dil. ; 17 Blank, several doses of
1st dil. ; 17 a, same, second proving ; 18, Dr. S., one dose of the Jo^h ; 19)

IHincl, — Exalted condition of the brain and special senses; memory
improved (third day),'. — Mind clear; everything seems very distinct (morn-
ing of second and fourth days),". — Almost impossible to write correctly;
drops out words and misspells (second day),*. — Memory seems affected ;
cannot remember anything an hour after it has happened ; unusual (fifth
day),'"'.

Mead. — Vertigo. Vertigo at 8 p.m. (second day),'". — Vertigo when
turning the head suddenly; fulness of the head (second day),^ — Vertigo,
with heat in the head (third day),'". — Vertigo and nausea on rising (third
day),". — Vertigo, and sleepless at night (first day),'"". — General Head.
[10.] Rush of blood quickly to the head on rising from a seat at 11 a.m.;
everything turned black before the eyes, and she nearly fell down (sixteenth
day),'"'. — -Congestion of the head (thirteenth- and fourteenth days),"^ —
Congestion of the head, painless, with strong pulsation of the vessels of the
neck (5 p.m., third day),'.— Sensation as if all the blood was trickling down
from the front to the back of the head (tenth day),'". — Lightness of head
(twelfth day),'". — Head dull all day, very nervous about it (seventh day),'"'-
— Head dull and heavy, with occasional pain in the forehead and eyes

(second day),"''. — Great paiu in the head, worse on the left side, at 7 p.m.

Fulness in the head, it feels too heavy, at 8 p.m. (third hour),". — [20.]
Fulness, as if the top of the head would rise off (fourth hour),". — Fulness
of the head all day; on stooping, it seemed as if the blood would spurt
from the nose; relieved at 10 p.m. (twelfth day),". — Headache at the base
of the brain, extending up and over to the vertex ; relieved by pressing
the head behind the orbits ; with flushed face and rheumatic pains in the

A.M., increased till 3 p.m., when it seemed as if it would burst (fifth day),"^
— Slight headache during the evening; a dull pain on both sides of the
forehead, with a sensation of fulness (second day),". — Forehead. Slight
pain in the forehead, and head is sore to the touch (fourth day),". — Slight
pain in the forehead just over the eyes; the pain increased during the day,
and at 8 p.m. it was felt all over the head and eyes ; the rush of blood to
the head and face caused a distressing fulness (ninth day),'"'. — Sensation
of fulness in the forehead, as if the brain were too large, during the day
(second day),". — Congestion, as if the blood would burst out of the fore-
head and eyes ; and at 11 a.m., while sitting in church, felt as if the blood

tends into the left eye, as if behind the pupil (third day),"^ — Pain in the
forehead above the eyes; increased and became very severe at noon; head
dull from 12 to 3 p.m., less severe after 1 p.m. ; pain in the head grew worse,
and seemed to go all through the head and eyes (fourth day),"^ — Fain in
the forehead just over the eyes, dull and heavy, from 12 to 4; it is sharp
and severe, and extends into the left eye; ceased at 4 p.m. (first and second
days),". — Sharp pain across forehead, painful to touch, with nausea (eighth
day),"*". — Sharp pain in the forehead just above the eyes; appeared in the
evening, after the second dose, and lasted all night,"'. — Headache in the
forehead on waking, worse at 8 a.m.; continues at intervals all day (sixth
day),". — Headache across the forehead, worse on the left side (sixth day),".
— Headache in forehead over the eyes at 10 A.M. (tenth day),". — Slight
headache across the forehead and eyes at various times during the day
(first day),""". — Dull headache across forehead and eyes on waking, worse
in the left eye (third, fourth, and fifth days),"^ — Temples. [40.] Pain
extending from the ear to the temples and the top of the head (fourth
hour),". — Throbbing in the temples, evening (second day),". — Vertex.
Full feeling across the top of the head at 10 a.m., increasing till 11 A.M., as
if all the blood in the body were in the head and face; at 12.25 p.m. it was
very severe, and extended iiitq the eyes, worse on the left side; ceased at 10
p.m. (second day),". — Top of the head feels as if it would burst at 10 a.m.
(fifth day),". — Sharp pain across the top of the head ; it is sore to touch ; the
soreness did not continue long, but the head ached from 1 till 5 p.m. (fifth
day),". — Parietals. Pain in the left side of the head, and a lifting, as if
the top were rising off (third day),". — Pain extending from the temple to the
occiput, on the left side, on rising in the morning, with a feeling of weakness ;
soreness of the scalp ; it smarts and burns (third day),". — Occiput. Woke
at 2 a.m. with pain at the base of the occiput and over the eyes ; very restless
till rising at 6 a.m.; mind clear, everything seemed very distinct (eighth
hour),'. — Slight pain in the back of the head, extending from the occiput to
the top of the head, with roughness and constriction in the throat (sixth

Severe headache in the left mastoid bone, extending obliquely across, by

darting pains, which start from the centre of the brain and move backward
in straight lines to the centre of the occijsital protuberance, aggravated by
motion (first day, first and second provings),'^

jEye. — Objective. Marked protrusion of the eyes, with dilated pupils
(fourth day),'. — Subjective. Dull, heavy feeling in eyes, with tendency
to close them, with the headache,". — Pain in the left eye and brow, extend-
ing across the forehead, continuing from 2 p.m. the rest of the day (fourth
day),". — Pain in the eyes, worse on closing them, but nearly as severe on
opening them (fourth day),'"*. — Sensation of fulness in the eyes, and a con-
fused, bursting-out feeling on looking steadily at any object, especially a
bright light; relieved by closing the lids; pupils dilated (first day),'". —
Eyes feel as if they would burst open or burst out of the head, worse on
turning the head ; lasted, very severe, all night (fifth day),"". — Congestion,
as if the blood were forcing its way out of the eyes (second day),"*"". — Sharp
pain in left eye, more while reading, with photophobia (fifth day),'". — ■
Lids. [60.] Peculiar twitching across the right upper lid, about 10 a.m.,
transient; in the left eye at 11 a.m. (second day),". — Jerking of the left
upper lid (third day),". — -Ball, Pressure on the cornea is very painful
(fourth day),"'^ — Ptipil, Pupils somewhat enlarged, with slight pain in
the balls (fourth day),".— Pupils dilated (fourth day),'; (first day),'"".—
Pupils much dilated, attract attention, 6 p.m. (fifth day),'l — Pupils dilated
more afternoons and mornings,'". — Vision. Smoky appearance of the room
(second day),'". — Dark clouds pass before the eyes, cannot see the letters
on the blackboard (second day),'". — Feels for another step when at the
bottom of the stairs (second day),'".

Ear. — [70.] Cold spot over the right ear, it feels like a stone, evening
(second day),'". — Pain extends into the ear from the parotid glands,'". —
Heading. Singing and snapping in left ear (second day),'". — Eoaring
in left ear on rising and in afternoon (third day),'"-

sections.label: Nose
sections.text:
Objective. A sore, like a cold-sore, inside the nostrils (fourth
day),". — Discharge (from nose) white and frothy, a little thicker than water
(thirteenth day),'". — Catarrhus nasi, with copious thick, yellow mucous
discharge,'. — Nose bled a little at 8 p.m. (fourteenth day),'"^— Bloody
discharge from nose several times (seventeenth day),'". — Subjective.
Nose stopped during morning (twelfth day),'". — [80,] Nose very dry and
burning (second day),\ — Feeling as if blood would spurt from the nose
(twelfth day),'".

sections.label: Face
sections.text:
Face flushed with the headache (fourth day),'. — Rush of blood
to face and head (ninth day),'"''. — Pain extends from the left eye to the
eye-tooth, like neuralgia (fourteenth day),'"'.

side (fifth day),^ — Tongue feels large, is coated white (third day),'"'. —
Tongue sore on the left side, raw, and red,"". — General 3Iouth. [90.]
Mouth dry (third day),"'. — Mouth dry and tastes like copper (third dayj,'^
— Roof of mouth dry ; cannot keep the tongue from constantly moving
over the roof of the mouth ; sensibility increased ; felt burnt (first hour),*.
— Mouth and fauces feel dry; constant inclination to swallow ; not relieved
by drinking (first hour),*. — Great dryness in the mouth and throat (first

Saliva. Commenced soon to secrete large quantities of saliva, which in
the morning was found to contain grayish lumps, afterwards the expecto-
ration was yellowish, and tasted salty; this appeared to be secreted just

each eructation,*^ — Saliva salt, like brine, continued several days,". —
Taste. Bad taste in the mouth (fifth day),*'; (sixth day),*\— [100.]
Taste fetid (third day),*". — Peculiar taste on the tongue posteriorly, extend-
ing into the throat, with immediate accumulation of saliva,^. — Taste acrid,
with nausea, like copper (first hour),*". — Taste metallic (first day),*''". — ■
Sour, metallic taste, lasts fifteen minutes after a dose, repeatedly,**. — Taste
like copper (third day),*^. — Taste like Lobelia or tobacco (first hour),*°-

sections.label: Throat
sections.text:
Sense of a plug in the throat, with scraping and dryness, a
feeling like that from tobacco (second hour),*". — Fulness in the throat,
which keeps him swallowing frothy mucus; the lump or fulness feels like
a small puff-ball ; not relieved by svallowing (morning of fifth day) ; this
returns in the evening after another dose, and is repeated after subsequent
doses,**. — Constriction and soreness of the throat, with difficulty of swallow-
ing solids, at 5 p.m. (third day),'. — [110.] Throat constricted and dry
(" similar to Lachesis "), (second day),". — Throat constricted and rough,
with pain in occiput, etc. (sixth hour),'. — Constricted feeling low down in
the throat, with slight nausea, causing a severe paroxysm of coughing (first
hour),^ — Neck feels too short by two inches (second and third days),'". — •
Uvula. Elongation of uvula (fifth day),*- — Fauces, Pharynx, and
(Esophagus. Mucous membrane of fauces dry, red, and congested (third
hour),*. — Dryness of posterior fauces, with hawking of mucus from posterior
nares (second day),'. — Intense burning in the oesophagus after an eructa-
tion, with a qualmish feeling, and an increase of saliva,**. — Fulness of the
fauces, with intense burning in the throat, fauces, and oesophagus,'^ — Con-
striction in the fauces, with dull pressure ; acrid taste, with nausea ; mouth
tastes like copper (first hour),*". — [120.] Rawness of pharynx from poste-
rior nares, left side, down to CESophasus, with sensation of a quantity of
mucus lodged in the nares and larynx, causing hawking ; hawking does
not seem to relieve it entirely, a portion only of clear viscid mucus coming
away (third and fourth days),*. — Swalloxving. Swallowing solid food
very difficult ; it is almost impossible to force solid food into the oesopha-
gus, semifluids more easily, and fluids easily swallowed (evening, second
day),". — External Throat. Pain in the submaxillary and parotid
glands, a stiff feeling in the parotids, and a pain extending from them into
the ear, at 8 p.m. (third hour),*". — Strong pulsation of the vessels of the
neck, with painless congestion of the head, at 5 p.m. (third day),'.

sections.text:
Appetite. Appetite not very good, an apparent indif-
ference to food ; very little satisfies ; what is eaten seems to sour on the
stomach, with eructations and a great deal of flatus (fourth day),'. — Ko
appetite for supper (second day),*". — No desire for breakfast ; the stomach

day),'". — Thirst. Thirst but slightly relieved by drinking, in the evening
(second day),". — JEi'HCtation. Constant desire to eructate, which he
dreads on account of the burning ; worse from smoking,'^ — *Eruetations of
hot, acrid fluid, which burns from the domach to the throat,^'. — [130.] * Eruc-
tations of burning hot gas from the stomach, causing a profuse secretion of

denly at 5.30 A.M., with very much nausea, which increased till he vomits

(third and fourth day),'. — [140.] Nausea shortly after rising, lasts till 10
A.M. ; it returned from 3 to 5 p.m., and again in the evening half an hour

fast ; returned and lasted till 10 a.m. (sixth day),". — *Nausea came on half
an hour after breakfast, not severe enough to cause vomiting, but very per-
sistent; relief for an hour in the afternoon, but returned at 2 p.m., and con-
tinued till he fell asleep, at midnight (third day),". — Nausea at 10.30 a.m.
(third day),'''. — Nausea continues till 11 a.m., when it gradually wears

— Nausea all the afternoon, but could not vomit (fourth day),''''\ — Nausea,
with retching and waterbrash, after eating (second day),^. — Nausea ; unable
to eat the usual breakfast, food seems loathsome ; sickness, almost to vomit-
ing ; relieved after eating (third day),'". — Nausea relieved by eating break-
fast (third day),'"''. — [150.] Nausea, stinging pain in the stomach, whirling
around at the pit of the stomach, with feeling of pressure (third day),'". —
Nausea and faint feeling, with a paroxysm of coughing as before (half an
hour after another dose),". — * Constant nausea all through the proving,"'. —
Constant nausea after 9 a.m., not affected by eating ; appetite good (second
day),". — Slight nausea, some flatus, and pain in the umbilical region (fourth
hour),". — Slight nausea and a constricted feeling low down in the throat,
causing a severe paroxysm of coughing (first hour),^ — Nausea continues,
and is aggravated by motion, especially on getting up in the morning, at 8
a.m. (second day),l — Stomach. Faintness in the stomach, lasted about
an hour, then gradually passed ofl^, leaving nausea, at 2 p.m., one half hour
after a dose (second day),'. — Heat in the stomach ; gradually disappeared
in a few minutes, 'I — Burning and weight in the stomach, aggravated by
smoking,'*. — [160.] Fulness and heat at the pit of the stomach, with nausea
and pain around the umbilicus (second day),'".

sections.label: Abdomen
sections.text:
Umbilical and Sides. Pain around the umbilicus
(second day),'". — Stinging pain in left side of abdomen, running into the
spermatic cord, in the morning (third day),'". — General Abdomen.
Bearing-down pain in the upper part of the abdomen (second day),'"'.—
Jerking and sharp cutting pain in the muscles of the abdomen ; waked
from sleep, with a scream, at midnight (second day),'". — Stinging pain in

the muscles of the abdomen, at 4 p.m. (second Jay)/°. — Mypofjastri/iim.
Pain across lower part of bowels on the right side (fourth day},'". — Colic in
the lower part of the abdomen, which nothing seemed to relieve ; stool
normal (second day),*.

Itectuni and Anns. — Protrusion of piles after a stool, very painful ;
had to sit down two or three times ; could not walk (thirteenth day),"^ —
Severe aching pain in the anus, waking out of sleep; relieved by stool, at
2.30 A.M. (fourth day),^— [170.] Tenesmus (third day),'"-

Stool, — Diarrhoea, preceded by sharp pain across the lower abdomen
(second day),"'. — Diarrhoeic stool, hurrying to the closet, without pain in
the rectum,". — Loose bowels, with transient pain in the abdomen after the
stool (fifth day),''. — Soft stool, with hard lumps, in the evening (second
day),'". — Soft, mushy stool at 9 a.m., again at 2 p.m. and 6 p.m. ; had
hardly time to get to the closet (second day),'*.

Urinary Organs. — Sladder. Bladder feels sore, as though it
had been overtaxed or strained ; must keep bent forward to take off the
pressure, in which position he feels much more comfortable (third day),". —
Micturition. Desire to urinate oftener than usual, but did not pass
much at a time; urine high-colored," "\ ■ — Frequent desire to urinate
(tenth day),". — Urine passed frequently and in large quantities (repeated
through two provings),". — [180.] '^Urinates frequently, day and night; the
attempt to retain it causes pain^^. — Called out of bed at 3 a.m. to' urinate ;
urine profuse and pale; urinated again at 8 a.m. ; copious, light lemon-color
(sixth day),". — Rises four times in one night to urinate; urine light straw-
color (third day),".— Seemed to be fast turning to urine, and running away
through his penis ; had to stop proving ; a renewal of the proving brings it
on again, with the sore stretched feeling in the bladder,". — Before proving,
troubled with a desire to urinate every half hour ; since taking the drug,
has urinated only four or five times in twenty-four hours,". — Urine.
Urine white and thick, in the morning (second day),TM. — Urine high-colored,
but clear (tenth day),''. — Uriue light-reddish, but clear (second day),'' ;
(third day),"''. — Urine somewhat increased ; passed with difficulty (fourth
day),'. — Urine scanty and high-colored (second and third day),". — [190.]
Urine normal in color and quantity, but has a greasy pellicle on the surface
(first day),*. — Urine cloudy and dark (first day),*.

Sexual Organs. — Menses more profuse than usual ; two days too
early,"'. — Menses scanty, seventeen days too late ; in the morning had pain
across the small of the back, and in the lower part of the abdomen ; menses
appeared at 11 p.m., with a very distressed feeling across the lower part of
the abdomen ; back pained all day and night ; flow scanty and pale,"

Mespiratory Organs. — Larynx. Dryness and burning of larynx
(after twelve hours, second day),'. — Dryness and rawness, extending to
larynx, the rim of the glottis being particularly affected (fifth day),'. —
Rawness and swelling increased, with spasm of the glottis, awaking me from
sleep and causing severe jsain and suffocation (fourth night),'. — Voice.
For an hour and a half after rising, my voice was entirely without control,
whispering and squeaking when expecting to speak loud ; croaking and
deep voice; this continued more or less through the day (sixth day) ; and
with the other symptoms gradually disappeared the day after,'. — Some
hoarseness ; sensitive to the cold air ; (here followed a cold, for which other
remedies were taken), (second day),^.— Cough and Bxjtectoration ,
Severe paroxysm of coughing, with slight nausea, caused by a constricted
feeling low down in the throat (first hour),'.— [200.] Spasmodic, ringing

cough, caused by irritation of the throat from hot eructations, aggravated
by smoking tobacco,''. — Dry cough all day (twelfth to fourteenth day),". —
Secretion of and a hemming up of small lumps of tough mucus of grayish
color (fifth day),\ — Hespirntioii. Sawlike, rasping sound of respira-
tion (fifth day), (took Bell. 1-"),^

sections.label: Chest
sections.text:
Left lung and back of the breast sore all day, but did not pain
(fifth day),'". — Pain in the lower part of the left side, extended around to
the back, soon passed off, after eating, at 6 p.m. (fourth day),'"'. — Woke
at midnight with a scream, and pain and cramp in the muscles of the left
side, with jerking and sharp cutting pain in the muscles of the abdomen
(second day),'". — Sharp, transient pain in the lower part of the left side, at
10.30 P.M. (second day),'". — At 9 a.m., a severe, sharp, cutting or sticking
pain in the upper third of the right side ; worse from motion ; most relief
from folding the arms across the chest ; it becomes so severe that he is
obliged to take Bryonia, which relieves him, but the side remains very sore ;
after another dose of Lactic acid, the pain and sorene-ss returned ; is com-
pelled to keep the arm close to the side to avoid pain ; it is very difficult to
put bis coat on or off; repeated in subsequent proving,'*. — Pain in the back
part of right breast at intervals during the morning, till 11 a.m., when the
pain extended to the axilla, which feels sore to the touch (fourth day),'". —
[210.] Pain in the back of the left breast, two or three times during the
day (sixth day),'". — Sharp pain in right breast at 11 a.m. (sixth day),'". —
Sharp pain darted through the lower part of the right breast at 1 p.m., and
continued at intervals during the afteruoon (fourth day),'". — Sharp pain in
back part of the left breast during the afternoon ; at 6 p.m., a similar pain
in the right breast, after which it felt sore to the touch ; soon passed away
(second day),'"-

Heartand Pulse. — IPrcecordiutn, The heart-sounds were clear
(sixth day),^°*. — Slight depression and constriction in the cardiac region ;
relieved by bending the chest forward ; in the forenoon (second day) and
repeated,'^. — Sharp pain around the heart, causing palpitation, a few min-
utes after 11.30 a.m. ; lasts till 2 p.m. (second day),'". — Pulse. The pulse
rose 12 beats (after three days),TM". — The pulse was 102 (sixth day),TM\ —
Pulse 98, full and soft,TM\— [220.] Pulse 96, full and soft,".— Pulse 90 and
full (third day),TM.— Pulse 90, feverish (third day),'^— Pulse 62, small and
feeble (second day, half an hour after a dose),'°.

Neck find liack. — Rheumatic pain in the right side of the neck and
right breast, worse from stooping the head ; continued about an hour (sixth
day),'". — Great distress in the region of the kidneys (tenth day),'". — Pain
in the lower part of the back and head all night ; the pain extended to the
shoulders, especially the right,'". — Pain in the small of the back at 11 a.m. ;
extends up the left shoulder and side of the neck ; did not last long in the
neck and shoulder, but continued in the back all day (second day),'". — •
Pain in the small of the back about noon ; continued all night (fourth and
fifth day),'"\ — Pain in the small of the back all night, could hardly lie in
bed (first and second day) ; extends to the shoulders (third day),'"\ — [230.]
Pain in the region of the kidneys, from 11 to 12 a.m. (fourth day),'". — On
retiring, a severe pain in the left lumbar region, more a weak feeling, which
is relieved by turning on to the side (first and second day),*. — Aching in
the lower part of the back, from 3 to 10 p.m. (first day),'". — Sharp pain
across the small of the back and shoulders, worse when walking (fifth
day),'". — Sore pain across the lower part of the back all day (second
day),'"^

Extremities in General. — The attempt to take the acid was
always followed by pains in the joiuts/\ — Pains in the joints, in the even-
ing (second day),TM. — Severe pain in various joints,'^'. — Acute pains in the
joints and flying pains about the limbs,TM. — After taking it for a week in
May, he was laid up with such severe joint-pains that I was called to visit
him and found hira in bed with pains in his elbows, shoulders, ankles,
knees, and, as he said, all over hini,^\ — [240.] He had a bad night from
pains in the joints, which disturbed him very much, and which came on
suddenly after midnight (fifth night) ; the next morning the metacarpo-
phalangeal and first phalangeal articulations of the first and second fingers
of each hand were found to be red, swollen, hot, and painful ; the slightest
movement aggravated the pain, and he could not on this account pick up
anything with his fingers ; the acid mixture was stopped, and in the even-
ing the pain in the knuckles was less, and the redness was diminished;
they were, however, still stiff; no other joints were affected (sixth day),TM\
— Elbows and knees painful and stiff,TM''

Superior Extremities, — Shoulder. Pain in the shoulder on
moving the arm, with soreness in the side (third day),'*. — Rheumatic pains
in both shoulders, running up the muscles of the neck to the mastoid pro-
cess, and into the ears,"*. — Wrist. Slight rheumatic pains in the wrist-
joint (half an hour),*. — Flying pains about the joints for four days, after
which he was disturbed at night by severe pain in the right wrist, which in
the morning was red, swollen, painful, and hot, and was a typical specimen
of a rheumatic joint,TM. — Hand. Small joints of both hands, wrists, and
in the last degree the elbows are red, swollen, and painful ; they seem
typical syoaptioras of acute rheumatic arthritis; in the evening both wrists,
the small joints of the fingers and the elbows are all red, hot, swollen,
tender, and painful (third day). Lactic acid was discontinued, the next
day the joints were better,*. — Pains returned in the knuckles in the even-
ing; they were swollen, red, and tender,TM\ — Fiilffers. Pain in the second
joint of the right thumb, at 1 p.m., for an hour (second day),"'. — Index
finger, right, swollen, two bright red spots on it, one between first and sec-
ond, the other between second and third joints; the last itched once or
twice during the day ; from 2 to 10 p.m., it itched and burned like a bee-
sting; on the fifth day it was sore between the first and second joints, but
not red ; between the second and third joints red, but not sore ; the red spot
looked like a blister," — [250.] Right index finger felt sore between the
first and second and also between the second and third joints ; these pains
continued during the proving, alternately appearing and disappearing,".

Inferior Extremities. — Thir/h. Pain in the thigh, and stinging
in the sartorius muscle (third day),'". — Soreness to touch along the track of
the right sciatic nerve, on getting out of bed ; lasts all day, pulsating con-
stantly, but slightly (fourth day),". — Knee. A swelling or redness of the
knees or other joints,^'. — None of the joints were swollen except the right
knee, which was faintly red, decidedly swollen, and very tender and pain-
ful; the other joints were simply stiff and painful on movement,^\ — Weak-
ness of the knees, and stinging in the joints (third day),'". — Great weakness
in the knees on going downstairs ; feels for another step at the bottom,
with vertigo (third day),". — He complained a good deal ef pain in the
knees, which had hitherto escaped (fourth day),TM. — Pain in the knees when
walking ; they cripple forward (evening, second day),". — Pain in the knee-
joints similar to neuralgic pains, at times extending to the toes, with a
thrilling sensation as if one's foot had been asleep (third day),". — [260.]

Pain in the patella (third day)/". — Eheumatic pains, dull yet sharp, in the
knee-joiut on moving the leg, at 7 p.m. (third day),^ — Sharp pain in the

Stinging pain in the knees, and inside the thighs (fourth day),". — Leg.
Cramp in the calf of the leg early in the morning, before leaving the bed,

(reneral Symptoms. — Objective. Great jerking of the muscles,
and rigor all over the body, in evening (second day),". — Spasm of different
muscles; it is difficult to eat or write (second day),". — Weakness on rising
in the morning, with pain in the head (third day),''. — Subjective. Sen-

he had walked a long distance, during and after motion (fourth day),'. — ■
Felt weak during the morning (fifth day),". — Felt sick all over; relieved
by eating lunch, at noon (third day),"^ — Rheumatic pains in the bones,
worse on motion (fourth day),'.

Skill. — Objective. Red spots on the left arm, left hip, left hand, in
the morning (third day) ; on the scrotum, with itching (third day),". —
Several distinct bright-red blotches (as large as a raspberry) on the anterior
portion of the lower third of the left leg, with slight burning, but no itch-
ing, relieved by cold, and by passing quickly from warm to cold, or cold
to warm ; the eruption is brightest at 8 a.m., fades in the middle of the
day, and grew lighter again during the evening ; brighter on pressure
(first and following days) ; eruption fades away from the periphery towards
the centre ; the centre remains bright till the fifth day, when it disap-
peared,'° ; in the second proving, these deep-red blotches reappear on both
legs, and extend almost over the thighs and lower limbs, to which they are
confined,'^*. — Elevations on the back like hives, with itching ; also itching
and redness on other portions of the body (eighth day),^ — Eruptions on
right arm and left leg, itch and burn,". — Papular eruption on the face and
hands (fourth day),'. — Small blisters on the hands," — [280.] Erysipela-
tous redness of left cheek and left side of nose, with small sore vesicles on
nose, in the morning (third and fourth day),\ — Subjective. Itching of
the body on going to bed, on account of cold from the clothes (third day),".
— Itching and burning on going out into cold air, with creeping and sting-
ing in left half of body, left arm, hand, and leg, in the evening (second
day),". — Itching is aggravated by scratching,'''. — Itching of the skin, re-
lieved by scratching,". — Itching on different parts, chest, back, abdomen,
and extremities (eighth day),^ — Itching and redness, not on exposed parts
of the body,**.

sections.label: Sleep
sections.text:
Sleepless, with vertigo (first day),"^ — Restless all night, could
neither lie still nor sleep, 'I — Does not sleep well ; restless ; backache all
night (sixth day),"'. — [290.] Did not sleep well; restless ; seemed to have
had dreams but did not remember them ; tired on waking (fifth day),"'\ —
Very restless at night (first day),'. — Very tired on -waking, with aching of
the limbs, as if she had not slept any (second day),""-

Fevef.— Chilliness. Cold and chilly at noon; transient (third
and sixth days),"". — Shivering in the muscles, with burning and sting-
ing in the left half of the body (third day),'".— Rigor all over, with
jerking of the muscles; cold feet; right hand cold, left hand hot; in the
evening (second day),'".— Feet cold, in the evening (second day),".—
Heat. The temperature showed no marked change until four or five days,

ach.— {Tobacco-smoking), Burning eructations; burning, etc., in stomach.

sections.label: Mind
sections.text:
Emotional. Lively mood (secondary action),''. — Merry
delirium, which began about midnight and increased until morning ; sang,
jumped about on his bed, and played all sorts of antics (boy),''". — In the
evening after grief, stupefying headache, violent contraction in the larynx,
inclination to weep caused by the grief; though Lactuca seems to cause
sadness with exalted fancies, so that the worst fears and apprehensions are
aroused by the merest trifles (after twelve hours),'. — Internal uneasiness,
anxiety (after eight hours),^ — Extremely ill-humored from the slightest
cause (second and third day),^. — Fretful mood, with disinclination to work
(second to eighth days),". — She is fretful, excited by trifles, and aroused to
anger (first day ),".-■- Very fretful but depressed mood (first day),'. — Peev-
ish mood (first day),'^ — Intellectual. [10.] Unusual disinclination to
work, ill-humor; it does not trouble him in bed (second day),'. — Dimin-
ished power of thought (after a quarter of an hour),''^ — Mental labor
cannot be accomplished ; the thoughts become confused ; or no connected
train of thought can be carried on (first hours),'.— Stupefaction,*.

sections.label: Head
sections.text:
Confusion and Vertiijo. Confusion of the head,'*"*';
in morning (second day),* ; (second morniug),".^Confusion of the head,
lasting twelve hours,'. — Confusion of the head in the morning, as after a
debauch (second to fifth day),'- — Confusion of the head, in the morning
after rising, with pressing from within outward in the forehead and orbits
(after eight hours),'. — Confusion and dulness of the head (after one hour),'*-
— Somewhat confused in the head (after one hour),'. — [20.] The head is
confused and heavy (second morning),'. — Confusion in the forehead (after
one hour),^ — Confusion and a feeling of heat in the forehead (while bruis-
ing the fresh herb),'. — Confusion in the forehead externally, alternately
more sensitive, now in the right, now in the left frontal eminence ; on stoop-
ing, there is at times short transient stitching thi'ough the left eminence
(second, third, and fourth days),*. — Confusion in the right side of the fore-
head, in the morning, for several minutes,^ — The head is befogged, dizzy,
though without impairment of the power of judgment,'. — Vertigo,*"*'; also
from the exhalations,'" TM ; (from 10 to 15 grains of Parisian Lactucarium)," ;
(from Lactucarium Genuinum),'l — Even the odor causes vertigo,". — Ver-
tigo ; it suddenly became black before the eyes ; the threads ran together
while sewing; but if she looked off of her work for some time vision be-
came better (after half an hour, and recurring several times during the

Guiding Symptoms the above. It does not seem, after

be said to impress this upon the memory and confidence
of any physician. Now, the why of this almost invari¬

as invariable amelioration from the same of Bryonia I
leave for those to explain who pretend to be able to do
so. Jt is, however, another proof of the value of mo¬

Lachesis has some peculiar symptoms of stool and anus.
There is an urging, or rather a ])ressing down, in the rec¬
tum, but it is worse when he attempts a stool; hurts so
that he must desist. It feels as if the anus were closed.

I'his is somewhat like the constjuit or rather frequent,
though ineffectual, urging to stool of Nux vomica; or like
the painful constricticni of Lycopodium, which cither pre¬
vents stool, or follows after an incomplete and unsatisfac¬
tory one. Another marked symptom is that the stools are
often very offensive, whether formed or not. Then, un¬
der Lachesis, we have Incmorrhages from the bowels, of
decomposed blood, which occur mostly during the course
of exhausting, acute diseases, like typhoid. Guernsey
gave this: “Flakes of decomposed blood, having form
and appearance of perfectly charred wheat straw, in
larger or shorter flat pieces ; ixjrtions more or less ground
up.” I have met such cases and Lachesis was very effi¬
cacious, not only in changing the character of the stool,
but bringing al>out general improvement, ultimating in
perfect recovery.

This remedy is often of great use in that very common
malady, hsemorrhoids ; and liere you have the constricted
feeling, whether the piles are external or blind, and some-


II9

times a beating or throbbing, or as the patient will per-
haps express it, a sensation of “little hammers” beating
in the rectum. All these symptoms and many more
show the aflinity of this remedy for the anus and rectum,
as they do also its power over disease of the whole ali¬
mentary tract.

This is also one of our best remedies in diseases of the
female generative organs. In the first place it is em¬
inently an ovarian remedy, and seems to choose by })refcr-
ence the left ovary. It is of use in simple ovarian neural¬
gia, and from that to actual tumors or even cancer (jf the
left ovary; or the trouble begins in the left and goes to
right ovary. (Rever.se Lycopodium.) lJut we may
have neuralgia, swelling, induration, suppuration, tumors
or cancer of one or both ovaries. Its action in uterine
troubles is also very marked. Here is a condition, as
expressed in Guiding Symptoms, that 1 have often veri¬
fied during climaxis; “Pains in uterine region increase at
times- more and more till relieved by flow of blood from
vagina; after a few hours or days, the same again, and
so on.”

In these cases you almost always have the intolerance
of least contact or pressure over the uterine region so
characteristic of this drug. The womb jirolapses, is at
times persistently congested, and obstinate uterine haem¬
orrhages repeatedly occur. There are hot flashes, hot ver¬
tex, pale face and fainting, uterine displacements of vari¬
ous kinds, and deranged capillary circulatit.n, all sej cf)m-
mon in females at the menoi>ause and especially htemor-
rhages. (See also Crotalus and Krcosotc.) Probably
there are not three remedies in the whole Materia Medica
so often indicated in troubles connected with this period.

120


as Lachesis. {Kreosote, post-climacteric diseases.) It
is often of great use in cancer of either the breasts or
uterus. In either ca.se the cancer puts on a bluish or
purplish appearance, and if open or fungoid bleeds easily,
a dark, decomposed blood. In case of bleeding, the imins
and suffering, as in the case of uterine haiinorrhage, are
temporarily relieved by it. We would be greatly crippled
in the treatment of these various ovarian and uterine
troubles without Lachesis.

The respiratory organs and chest also come under the
influence of this drug. Paralysis of the vocal chords,
causing loss of voice; larynx is sensitive to least touch; it
causes suffocation ; it is one of our best remedies in des¬
perate cases of croup, where the child gets worse in sleep ;
seems to sleep into it. Spasm of the glottis ; sensation of
something running from neck to larynx, stopping the
breath. It has great shortness of breath when walking,
especially in old topers and in heart affections, when this
condition is always the guide to its use. ‘'The least thing
coming near the mouth or nose interferes with breathing;
tears off the collar or everything about the neck, throat or
chest, because it suffocates.”

Asthma with the same symptoms, has sudden flushes of
heat or orgasm of blood ; must loosen clothes to prevent
suffocation; threatened paralysis of the heart or lungs;
dry hacking cough, aggravated by touching throat or
larynx, also cough during sleep, without awakenitig or
being con.scious of it. Here it often cures very obstinate
cases of cough after Chamomilla has failed, which also
has this symptom. For the short dry cough sympathetic
with heart troubles, Lachesis is often useful. Cough
with pain in anus, or stitches in pile tumors. One of our


121

best remedies in typhoid pneumonia or typhoid fever with
lung complications.

Now look out for the Lacliesis tongue in these cases.
Lachesis is also one of our most useful remedies in heart
troubles, acute or chronic, the peculiar suffocation, cougli
and aggravation from constrictions being the guiding
symptoms.

No remedy more profoundly impresses the nervous sys¬
tem than this. In the first place it causes trembling, not
from fright or excitement, but from extreme weakness.
In this it resembles Gclsemiiim; both have great trem¬
bling of the tongue on trying to protrude it. With both
remedies the whole body trembles ; but with Lachesis she
feels faint, as if .she must sink right down. 'J'his great
prostration is both mental and physical, and she does not
improve from rest or sleep, but on the contrary is worse
in the mouiiny after sleeping. With this prostration
there are often pain or other troubles with the heart;
nausea, pale face and vertigo. Now if this thing goes
on the next stage suj)crvcnes and paralysis is the end of it.
The paralysis is generally left-sided, as arc the majority
of complaints of Lachesis, which is pre-eminently a hft-
sided 1 emedy. This paralysis may come on as a result of
apoplexy or cerebral exhaustion; if the latter, there is still
great hope of a jM^rfect cure by a judicious use of Lache¬
sis. Of course if the lesion is too extensive in apoplexy,
and the extravasation of blood too great, there is little
hope; but some apparently most dcsi>erate ca.ses do re¬
cover even then. It is recommended in epilepsy and loco¬
motor ataxia, but I have never seen good effects from it.

There is, however, another place in which I have seen
it accomplish much and that is in the languor, weariness

122


and prostration from hot weather. The head not only
aches^ but the whole body seems prostrated by sun heat.
(Antim. crud., Gclscminni, Glonoine, Natmm carb.,
Natrmn m.)

Worse after sleep, or rather the patient sleeps into an
aggravation, is a genuine characteristic of this remedy, no
matter what the enemies of Lachesis say of it. On this
line there is one particular symptom to which I wish to
call attention, i. e., “As soon as the patient falls asleep,
the breathing stops.” This is as Hering expresses it. I
have oftencr found it tliis way; the patient cannot go
clear olT into sleep, because just on the verge of it the
breath stops and he wakens catching for breath. This is
often found in heart troubles, functional or organic, and
is very distressing. Grindclia robusta has a similar
symptom. (Also Digitalis.)

I once had a case of very obstinate constipation in an
old syphilitic case. He was at last taken with very severe
attacks of colic. The pains seemed to extend all through
the abdomen, and always came on at night. After trying
various remedies until I was discouraged, for he “got no
l)etter fast,” he let drop this expression, “Doctor, if I
could only keep awake all the time, I would never have
another attack.” I looked askance at him. “I mean,”
.said he, “that I sleep into the attack, and waken in it.” I
left a dose of Lacncsis 200. He never had another at¬
tack of the pain, and his bowels became perfectly regular
from that day and remained so. I could give more cases
where this .symptom has led me to the cure of ailments of
different kinds. It is enough to .say that I have no hesita¬
tion in adding my testimony to that of others as to the
value of this symptom. I think I have said enough about


123

the different s3miptoms of Lachesis to indicate that it is
one of the most useful remedies in typhoid fever. I will
only add here that it is generally in the second or third
week of the disease that it is found indicated. This is
one of the differences between it and Gclscmmm. For
the trembling and weakness of Celscmiuin come early,
and if recognized then Celscmimn can abort the disease
at once. Of course the sensoriurn, tongue, mouth, throat,
abdominal and stot)l symptoms already spoken of, espe¬
cially the sleep symptom, help to decide the choice be¬
tween Lachesis and other remedies.

Now upon the tissues. We have swelling on all parts
of the body, and one of the most characteristic conditions
is the color of them. They are bluish verging onto black.
{Tarantula Cub., Anthracinum.) 1 never see a swelling
of that color but Lachesis immediately comes to my mind,
and then if I find that they cannot bear to have them
touch-ed, they are so sensitive, even a poultice is unbear¬
able, becau.se it is so heavy, that settles it. I give Lachesis
